speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Incus Dislocation (Recurrent Patulousness/Articular Fracture)
The combination of shooting ear pain specifically triggered by chewing (eating) and pain with earrings following a tympanoplasty is highly suggestive of a mechanical issue with the ossicular chain, such as an incus dislocation, rather than a simple infection. Have you noticed any change in your hearing sensitivity or fullness in the ear since the surgery?
